name: Worldwide stations
source: NOAA Worldwide Marine Radiofacsimile Broadcast Schedules (7 March 2025); NWS USCG broadcast pages; 47 CFR 80.1077 (GMDSS); Australian Bureau of Meteorology; Priyom (French Navy, HFGCS); M7SPI list after Priyom (Russia, 2022); G4NSJ (Volmet, LDOC); Milcom Monitoring Post (NAT, 2015); hfunderground wiki (DWD RTTY, ZLM); udxf.nl (HFDL); Wikipedia (time signals, long wave at September 2026, broadcast bands); ARISS station status, 27 October 2026 (ISS); AMSAT FM and linear satellite frequency summaries, 31 October 2026 (satellites); oz7igy.dk and GB3NGI's keeper (beacons); Motorola Solutions and the PMR446 and LPD433 channel plans (licence-free bands).
note: For listening only: nothing here is yours to transmit on, and most is someone's safety or working traffic. Some countries, the UK among them, make it an offence to listen to messages not meant for you or to pass them on. These lists come from public and hobby sources of varying age, so a flag doesn't promise a signal.

stations.label: RS95S

stations.label: CAS-3H

groups.name: Satellites: linear transponders

stations.label: JO-97

stations.label: TO-108

stations.label: AO-7

stations.label: AO-73
stations.note: FUNcube-1. Passband 145.950-145.970. Works in eclipse

stations.label: FO-29
stations.note: JAS-2. Passband 435.800-435.900. Runs to a schedule, in sunlight
